title: The $21.3 billion holiday loan

lines: that U.S. shoppers are set to borrow through 'buy now, pay later' — just to cover the holidays.
Adobe projects a record $275.1 billion in U.S. online holiday spending this year, up 6.7%.
A record $21.3 billion of it rides on buy now, pay later.
Four payments — and interest if you miss one. (Adobe Analytics)
In Canada, it's the reverse: 56% say inflation is reshaping their holiday plans.
Average spending fell $64 to $911. (Retail Council of Canada x Leger)
A record sales number isn't a record good year — sometimes it just means more of it was borrowed.
Buy now, pay later, or cash this year?

source_line: Sources: Adobe Analytics; Retail Council of Canada x Leger, 2026
caption:
About $21.3 billion — that's what U.S. shoppers are set to put on 'buy now, pay later' this holiday season, a record, inside a record $275.1 billion in online spending, up 6.7% (Adobe Analytics).

BNPL splits a purchase into four payments; miss one and fees and interest start — which is how holiday gifts quietly become January debt. In Canada it's the opposite: 56% say inflation is reshaping their plans and average spending fell $64 to $911 (Retail Council of Canada x Leger).

My take: a record sales number isn't a record good year — sometimes it just means more of it was borrowed.

Using buy now, pay later this year, or paying cash? 👇
